question: Had the dinosaur-killing asteroid struck a random spot on Earth, how likely was a mass extinction?
answer: About one in eight, by one model. Kaiho and Oshima traced the killing darkness to soot from rocks rich in oil and organic matter, which underlie only about 13% of Earth's surface. The shelf off Yucatán was one. A strike almost anywhere else, open ocean included, would on their estimate have spared the dinosaurs' world.
move: Ask how the same blow would have landed somewhere else.
trap: A 10 km asteroid seems catastrophic wherever it happens to land.
reference: Kaiho & Oshima, Site of asteroid impact changed the history of life on Earth: the low probability of mass extinction, Scientific Reports, 2017
